questions.question: Q: What are the four principal parts of a Latin verb?

points.text: First person singular present active indicative, present infinitive, first person singular perfect active indicative, and perfect passive participle. Example: laudo, laudare, laudavi, laudatus.

questions.question: Q: How do you identify which conjugation a verb belongs to?

points.text: By the characteristic vowel in the present infinitive (second principal part): 1st -are (a), 2nd -ere (e), 3rd -ere (short e/consonant), 4th -ire (i).

questions.question: Q: What are the present tense personal endings?

points.text: -o/m (1st singular), -s (2nd singular), -t (3rd singular), -mus (1st plural), -tis (2nd plural), -nt (3rd plural).

questions.question: Q: How is the imperfect tense formed?

points.text: Add -ba- plus personal endings to the present stem. Example: laudabam (I was praising), laudabas (you were praising).

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between active and passive voice?

points.text: Active: the subject performs the action (puella laudat — the girl praises). Passive: the subject receives the action (puella laudatur — the girl is praised).

questions.question: Q: How is the perfect tense formed?

points.text: Use the perfect stem (third principal part minus -i) plus perfect endings: -i, -isti, -it, -imus, -istis, -erunt. Example: laudavi (I praised).

questions.question: Q: Name three irregular Latin verbs and their meanings.

points.text: Sum (to be), possum (to be able), eo (to go). Also: volo (to want), nolo (not to want), malo (to prefer).
